collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: Miss ~30 calls a week during jobs at Ortiz Roofing in Dallas

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Totally hear you — there’s a lot of junk out there right now.  

So before I even try to “convince” you… what kind of business are you running, and where do missed calls or lost leads show up for you today?
User: Ortiz Roofing in Dallas. Miss ~30 calls a week during jobs. How do I know this isn't recorded?
Agent: Got it, thanks for being straight with me.  

This isn’t some dumb recording — it listens and responds in real time like a receptionist, so if a homeowner calls about hail damage at 8:37 pm, it can actually answer questions, book an inspection, or grab photos… instead of them just hanging up.  

When those 30 calls a week hit you while you’re on a roof, what usually happens — do they go to voicemail, or just ring out and disappear?
User: They usually go to voicemail, but I'm skeptical. Who's controlling this thing, and where does the data go?
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense to be skeptical, especially with all the AI hype.  

So, two parts: Jay’s team at Dialux configures and controls the system for you (it only does what we set it up to do: answer, qualify, book, send you the details), and call data is stored securely in our system and/or your CRM, not sold or shared — it’s just to make sure every caller gets handled and you can see exactly what happened.  

When those calls hit voicemail now, do people usually leave a message, or are you seeing a lot of hang‑ups and “we already booked someone else” later?
User: They usually go to voicemail, but I'm skeptical. Who's controlling this thing, and where does the data go?
Agent: Totally fair questions.  

I’m Linda, an AI assistant on Jay’s team at Dialux — Jay’s the human who actually sets these systems up for roofers — and the “brain” only does what we configure: answer calls, ask your questions, book estimates, and send you the caller details; call recordings/transcripts live in our secure system and, if you want, push into tools you already use (like your CRM or calendar), and we don’t sell or share that data.  

On those voicemails right now, are you actually able to call most people back the same day, or do some just never get a response because you’re slammed on jobs?
User: Some voicemails slip through the cracks when I'm busy. Who besides you gets to see or hear those recordings?
Agent: Makes sense — if you’re buried on a job, it’s easy for a few to just vanish.  

Outside of you and anyone on your team you choose to give access to, it’s just Jay’s small Dialux team for support and setup — nobody else is listening in, and we’re not selling or sharing those calls; you can also limit who on your side can see recordings versus just summaries.  

Given a few voicemails are slipping through now, has anyone ever walked you through what that might be costing you in actual jobs each week?
User: No one's done the math for me. Tell me how much I might be missing out on, but keep it clear.
Agent: Got it, let’s keep it super simple and use your real numbers.  

First one: out of those 30 calls a week that hit you during jobs, how many would you say actually go to voicemail instead of getting answered live — more like 10, 20, or almost all 30?
User: Almost all 30 end up in voicemail. I'm usually up on a roof or with a customer.
Agent: Got it, so we’ll use 30.  

Next piece: if you actually answered those calls live, what percentage do you think would turn into a booked job or inspection — maybe 30%, 50%, 70%?
User: I'd say about 40% of those missed calls could turn into booked jobs or inspections.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use 40%.  

Last piece: for a typical roofing job you get from these calls — whether it’s a repair or a full replacement — what’s a rough average value in dollars?
User: Typical job goes for about $1,800. But again, how do I know you're not just a bot?
Agent: Thanks for the numbers — I’ll hit your question and the math, both.  

I am a bot, yeah — I’m Linda, an AI on Jay’s team — but I’m just here to run through this with you; the real “is this garbage or not?” test is how the system handles your calls.  

Using your numbers: if you answered and booked just 40% of those 30 missed calls at $1,800, that’s about $21,600 a week walking away — does that sound in the ballpark of what you’re seeing, or does it feel high to you?
User: $21,600 sounds about right, but I need to know who's really handling my calls, not just AI.
Agent: Totally fair — if someone’s touching your customers, you want to know who.  

Under the hood, it’s a system that answers like a trained office person, but the *humans* behind it are Jay and his small team: they script it with you, listen to sample calls, tweak how it talks, and you get a dashboard where you can review or override anything at any time.  

Since we’re talking about roughly $93K a month at risk, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay this week so you can see exactly how it behaves on *your* roofing calls before you trust it with a single customer?
User: Alright, but I'm still cautious. Let's schedule that walkthrough. I want to see this in action first.
Agent: Nice, that’s exactly the right mindset — “trust, but verify.”  

First thing I’m missing is your first name, just so Jay knows who he’s meeting with — what should we put down for you?
User: Just put me down as Sam. But remember, I’m watching closely for any signs of trickery.
Agent: Got it, Sam — fair warning taken.  

And your last name, spelled slowly so I don’t butcher it?
User: Ortiz, O-R-T-I-Z. Simple, right? Make sure you get it right, I'm not playing around with my business name.
Agent: Ortiz with a Z — loud and clear.  

So, for Jay’s walkthrough, would you rather do later today or tomorrow, Central time?
User: Tomorrow works better, Central time. But remember, I’m skeptical until I see how this actually works.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you, Sam.
Agent: Sam, you’re all set — we’ve got you booked tomorrow at 10:45 Central for a 20-minute walkthrough with Jay. You’ll get a text in a bit with the confirmation and a link in case you need to reschedule.

There’s nothing to sign on that call — it’s just to see it in action on roofing calls and pressure-test it however you want.

Anything else you need from me before we hang up?

Alright, really glad you called in, and I respect you being cautious. Jay’s looking forward to meeting you tomorrow. Have a great rest of your day — bye!
